{"concern":"core","designation":"internal","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"Context cost is MEASURED and budgeted, not estimated at design time","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"REASSESSED 2026-07-28, same day, on Anthony's instruction not to treat reflow's workflows as canon. First written as "context consumption is modelled so a path that will not fit is knowable before it is walked", arguing from reflow's design-time estimation. The FINDING is mine and stands; reflow's MECHANISM is the weak half, and the name now says which.

THE FINDING, measured against reflow2's own design and independent of any prior art: DEPENDS_ON declares a coupling-weight facet whose schema comment states its purpose — "weight is a STRENGTH (higher = tighter); invert to a cost for shortest-path/closeness" — and over 3,250 edges, 232 carry weight_basis while ZERO carry weight, frequency or data_volume. The facet is declared and wholly unpopulated, which also explains req:edge-defaults-do-not-assert rather than merely repeating it: weight_basis asserts "estimated" over an absent weight because weights were meant to be there.

WHY DESIGN-TIME ESTIMATION IS THE WEAK PART. reflow made context_consumption a function attribute and the primary edge weight, published estimation guidelines (read_workflow_file 5000-15000 tokens, generate_architecture 5000-15000, and so on), summed along paths, and flagged CRITICAL above 160k. Three problems. (1) The estimates go stale the moment anything changes and nothing ever re-derives them, so the graph accumulates confident numbers nobody has checked — the shape this project keeps rediscovering. (2) They are model-specific: 160k was reflow's environment, tokenisers and context windows differ, and hardcoding one number as a law is the asserting default req:defaults-do-not-assert forbids. (3) Real consumption is dominated by what static structure cannot see — how much a tool actually returns, how many rounds a negotiation takes, what the user pastes in. A statically-summed path cost would be precise and wrong.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WANTED, and reflow2 already has most of the vocabulary. MEASURE rather than estimate: real sessions produce real costs per tool call and per skill, and weight_basis already distinguishes estimated / evidence / measured — further evidence the facet was designed for observed values, not guesses. Then BUDGET at runtime against what is left, which composes with cap:bounded-reads (a read that would not fit answers with a bounded page and says what it left out) and cap:tool-search (finding a tool on a surface too large to hold) rather than replacing them. A measured cost also feeds req:friction-has-a-baseline honestly, since "this got more expensive across a release" is a regression the baseline should catch.

An estimate is defensible only as a SEED for something never measured, and must read as estimated — which is exactly what weight_basis is for. Fixing the edge default and populating the facet remain two answers to one question and should be decided together. Found 2026-07-28 reviewing 99-meta_analysis.json; reassessed the same day.","status":"proposed"}
